Project-C identified a risk that the paint and varnish chemicals it is planning to use may cause mildly toxic emissions which may cause the site to be shut down for a week. Project-D identified a risk that if certain technical specifications are not specified in time, the commissioning of the machines may get delayed. Which risk should you (the program manager) be most concerned about?
choices: A. Project-C
B. Project-D
C. Project-B
D. Project-A

text: Which of the following statements about closure of programs correctly reflects when a program should be closed?
choices: A. Program D is being closed because most of the team members associated with the program have been let go
B. Program A is being closed because all the projects associated with it are completed
C. Program B is being closed because the program manager feels it has fulfilled its objectives in delivering benefits to the organization
D. Program C is being closed because the program steering committee felt the benefits forecast did not justify continued investment in the program

text: A program is in the preparation stage and planning is in progress. It is an internal program for the organization meant to improve operational efficiencies and the directive from senior management is to keep a close eye on the program costs. The projects within the program have given their schedules and resource requirements to the program manager. What is the most appropriate step for the program manager at this stage?
choices: A. Figure out if there is an opportunity to crash the schedule of the projects
B. Find out which components can be executed in parallel to reduce the program duration
C. Figure out opportunities to integrate the inputs and outputs of the projects to rationalize the use of resources
D. Determine the benefits likely to be realized from the program vis-à-vis the cost to be incurred

text: A program has many projects. The dependencies among the projects is complex. The program is time constrained. The program’s components is also heavily dependent on vendors and the program manager is trying to standardize the procurement policies across the program. Which type of contract is least appropriate for this program?
choices: A. Revenue share
B. Fixed Price
C. Cost reimbursable
D. Time and Material

text: One of the projects within a program has the goal of developing a tool to automate the generate PMIS reports in order to save time. The project manager would like to develop a charter. The project manager asked the manager of the program to specify the metrics to determine the success criteria for the project. How should the program manager proceed?
choices: A. Ask the project manager to develop a detailed business case and supply estimated RoI so that the baselines can be set up
B. Use historical data to establish the expectations in terms of cost and time
C. Discuss with the program steering committee in order to come up with the measures
D. Specify the expectations in terms of simplification, reduction of errors and savings in terms of time and cost, so that the measures can be derived

text: The goal of your program is to come up with a suite of software products that work together to provide the customers comprehensive views on their IT infrastructure. The suite comprises 15 different products, which share a common web-based dashboard and the data model. About a month from the launch, the marketing team has already started making presentations and accepting bookings for the software. At a readiness check meeting, you discover that one of the products responsible for reporting fails to function in certain conditions. The project manager tells you it would take about 6 months to fully address this issue. Who is responsible for deciding the most appropriate action in this case?
choices: A. The project manager of the faulty product
B. The marketing department after surveying the customers about what they would prefer
C. The program steering committee
D. The program manager and the marketing department

text: A project manager tells you that the quality requirements on his project are too stiff and he can only meet them up to 80%. You know that this project has a challenging technical environment which your organization doesn’t have much expertise in. What should you do?
choices: A. Call for a meeting of quality experts to brainstorm on possible means of improving the adherence to quality standards
B. Raise a change request to change the quality specs and approach the program steering committee
C. Examine the impact of the reduction in level of quality on the other projects and overall program benefits
D. Consider if the project can be outsourced to an organization which has the technical expertise needed to meet the quality requirements

text: A program manager is working on creating and securing authorization for a Program charter. Which of the following activities make sense for the program manager to perform at this stage?
choices: A. Figure out the possible sources of funding and expectations of the people who will likely fund the program
B. Initiate studies to come up with high level estimates for cost and time
C. Perform an initial risk assessment for the program
D. Establish a structure for governing the program when it gets authorized

text: Midway through a program, the VP of the Information Technology department threatens to pull resources from a component of the program saying she does not agree with the program’s objectives and that it is no longer a priority for her department. You have tried to reason with her before and getting cooperation from her department has always been problematic. What should the program manager do?
choices: A. Call for a meeting of all project managers to discuss what can be done under the circumstances
B. Note this as a program level risk and take it up at the steering committee meeting next month
C. Send the VP a copy of the charter which was signed off by the program steering committee and remind her of her department’s responsibilities
D. Inform the program steering committee and ask them for advise

text: A software development program comprises of several projects which have varying levels of complexity and duration. The program manager is very conscious of the need to achieve a high level of quality. Which quality policy can he think about imposing at the program level?
choices: A. All the deliverables on all projects will be subject to standardized acceptance tests
B. All project plans should follow the same template so that they can be read easily
C. 100% of the code written should undergo code review on all projects
D. All projects should follow ISO 9001:2000 standards

text: The program manager is about to initiate a project within the program and is working with the project manager on developing a charter. The project delivers an important product in the product suite that will be launched by the organization. The project manager thinks she would need additional help with a new technology and would like to hire team members either on full time or contract basis. The program manager had not budgeted for this and the program is tight on cost and time. How should the program manager proceed?
choices: A. Instead of hiring headcount, explore the possibility of training the existing team members on the new technology
B. Allow the team additional time for absorb the technology and work on the product development activities
C. Ask the project manager to provide detailed justification for the request and let her present to the program steering committee
D. Find a way to provide the necessary resources for the project by adjusting the program plan

text: Company A and B are both US based pharmaceutical companies. A has outsourced some research work to a biotech firm in India, and B is using contract teams in Philippines. Company A acquired company B and would like to standardize on one outsourced vendor. As a program manager in company B, what should your stand be?
choices: A. Make a visit to India to evaluate the contractor that company A is using
B. Come up with alternatives for contracting for the merged company
C. Migrate some of your projects to the India-based outsourcer and document lessons learnt
D. Ask your management to protect your program by retaining the services of your regular contractor

text: A program manager was working with ABC IT systems - an organization contracted to develop a set of IT systems for the customer facing services of the local municipal body. During a phase gate review, one of the members of senior management asked how the organization (ABC IT Systems) can leverage this assignment to developing marketing collateral. Which of the following would be the most meaningful metric to track attainment of the benefit of developing marketing collateral development?
choices: A. Number of new prospects identified
B. Number of brochures and white papers published
C. Number of press releases issued
D. Number of presentations made

text: A program manager is part of a matrix organization. She leads a team of project managers, all of whom belong to one or the other functions or lines of business (LoB). Whilst they are all committed to the program, they are also accountable for the projects they are performing to the functions. The program manager herself happens to be a part of one of the LoB’s, which contributes the most to the program’s budget and reports to the Director of that LoB. What is the biggest challenge that the program manager will have in this situation?
choices: A. Getting the functions to define scope of their projects
B. Communication across the project teams
C. Getting a charter for the program
D. Finding resources to manage the program

text: A government owned shipyard is building a large cruise ship. This is a highly complex initiative that is expected to take up to 7 years. The ship is intended to join a fleet of other ships that serve customers in a specific geographic region. Some of the components of this task are as follows. Design and construction of the hull, design and construction of the suites and entertainment areas, building the engine and turbines, electric generator, etc. From the description provided, this seems to be an example of:
choices: A. A project with several sub-projects
B. A program with several projects, because all projects have a common budget
C. A program with several projects, because it has clearly outlined benefits
D. A portfolio because it addresses a niche market
